name: Zabbai
overview: Zabbai is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Baruch. His tribal affiliation and other personal details are not recorded in Scripture. The limited information about him centers on his paternal relationship, highlighting his presence in the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Zabbai is a proper name that possibly means 'G-d has given.' This meaning, while not explicitly stated as given by God, reflects a common theophoric element found in Hebrew names, indicating a recognition of divine provision.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Zabbai as the father of Baruch, establishing a direct paternal link. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented, and his genealogy remains otherwise unspecified.
scriptureSignificance: Zabbai's significance lies in his connection to Baruch, who is mentioned in the context of Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild Jerusalem. Though Zabbai himself is not the focus, his mention serves to identify Baruch's lineage, contributing to the historical record of those involved in the restoration of the city.
